speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing significant symptoms including fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To better understand what might be causing this, can you tell me how long you've been feeling this way and if you've noticed any fevers or changes in your appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; those four weeks of "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss) combined with abdominal pain and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy are very concerning. Have you noticed any changes in your bowel movements, such as constipation or pain relief after passing stool, or any skin rashes? Also, have you had any recent fevers or drenching sweats specifically at night?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The new finding of a fixed, painless neck mass is highly suspicious for malignancy. To evaluate the extent of this disease, I need to see what's happening internally.

REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with contrast
REQUEST TEST: LDH (Lactate Dehydrogenase)
REQUEST IMAGES: Full body PET scan

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma
